notes: Shopify store (Indian lifestyle/home+fashion retailer). robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (general 'Allow: /' plus standard Shopify private-path blocks); HTTP-first access worked throughout, no browser needed. Full discovery: fetched main-nav mega-menu from homepage HTML (top-level: HOME, WOMEN, MEN, GIFTING, JEWELLERY, ACCESSORIES; 86 unique /collections/ links surfaced in current nav+footer), and enumerated the FULL backend collections.json (5 pages, 1247 total collections) filtered against the seasonal/festival keyword list (Christmas, Xmas, Diwali, Holi, Rakhi/Raksha Bandhan, Navratri, Dussehra, Eid, Ganesh Chaturthi, Janmashtami, Pongal, Onam, Durga Puja, Karwa Chauth, Makar Sankranti, Baisakhi, New Year, Valentine, Easter, Thanksgiving, Mother's/Father's Day, Festive, Holiday, Wedding Season, etc.) -> 115 keyword hits reviewed individually. Only ONE genuine keyword-only hit for Holi/Eid/Navratri/Ganesh/etc: zero -- none of those festivals have any collection on the site at all. Candidates investigated by sampling actual products.json content (not just title/URL), per the mandatory false-positive check: 'diwali' (collections.json count 113, real products.json enumeration 88 -- inflated count, cross-checked), 'xmas' (count 113, real 107), 'christmas-new-year' (count 88, real 71), 'christmas-gifting' (17), 'christmas-treehouse-edit' (9), 'new-year-looks' (9), 'festive-decor' (45), 'holiday-shop' (count 319, real 216), 'mothers-day' (count 143, real 134), 'wedding' (nav item, gifting-occasion not a calendar holiday), 'wedding-season' (37). Total catalog size (collections/all) = 2646 products, so none of these individually exceed the 20-30% red-flag threshold, but the CONTENT test (mandatory per task instructions) failed decisively for every one of them: sampled title lists are near-entirely generic catalog items shared across multiple 'different' holiday collections (mugs, vases, trays, planters, incense, cushion covers, kurtas, dresses, jewellery, sweaters, totes) with only isolated incidental occasion-adjacent items (a few Torans, a diya set, one 'Alphabet A Charm'); zero Christmas ornaments/wreaths/stockings/tree-decor/Santa items, zero Diwali diya/rangoli-majority assortment, zero Easter/Valentine content anywhere on the site. 'Chandni Chowk Kurta' and other identical SKUs recur across the Diwali, Christmas-New-Year and Wedding-Season lists -- proof these are the SAME generic 'giftable/festive-looking' assortment re-labelled under different holiday-named URLs each marketing season, exactly the false-positive pattern this task warns about. None of these collections (diwali, xmas, christmas-*, festive-*, holiday-shop, mothers-day, new-year-looks, wedding-season) are linked anywhere in the live main navigation or footer -- they are orphaned backend collections, not part of the site's presented taxonomy today (2026-09-04, off-season for Christmas/Diwali so some seasonal rotation is expected, but the content test independently disqualifies them regardless of nav timing). Per rules the nav-taxonomy signal and the content-specificity signal must both support inclusion; here neither does, for any of them. All excluded. The ONE genuine exception: 'Rakhi' (handle /collections/rakhi, title 'Rakhis') IS a live, currently-active main-nav item, nested under the JEWELLERY menu and visually highlighted (custom accent colour) as an in-season promoted category -- consistent with Raksha Bandhan having just passed (Aug 2026). Sampled its full product list (84 items returned by products.json): literally every single title is '<Name> Rakhi' / '<Name> Rakhi Set' / '<Name> Charmlet' -- a rakhi is exclusively a Raksha Bandhan item, so this passes the content test unambiguously; no ambiguity to flag. qty: collections.json products_count field reports 145 (inflated, per the known Shopify trap); cross-checked against both the rendered PLP ('84 Items' / 'Total items 84' badges visible in page HTML) and the raw products.json enumeration (84) -- both agree, so 84 is used as the exact qty, evidence recorded accordingly. No sub-tabs or child collections found on the Rakhi PLP itself (checked rendered HTML for internal links -- only self-link present), so this is recorded as a single leaf row, not a grouping node. Other rakhi-named backend collections found via collections.json enumeration (Rakhi Bundles, Rakhi Alphabet Series -Aqua/-Purple/-Green, Mandovi Rakhi) are not linked from the live Rakhi PLP or main nav -- treated as internal/legacy sub-collections, not presented site categories, and excluded to avoid manufacturing sub-rows the site itself doesn't present. No multilingual/regional-language navigation found (site is English-only storefront). Checked global.nicobar.com link in footer -- same Shopify backend/brand, not investigated separately per single-domain scope. Final result: exactly one genuine Seasonal category found -- Raksha Bandhan / Rakhi.

rows.evidence: Live main-nav item (JEWELLERY > Rakhi, accent-highlighted as in-season). Rendered PLP shows 'product-count-top">84 Items' and 'product-count-total-item">84'; products.json?limit=250 enumeration confirms 84 products, every title of the form '<Name> Rakhi' / '<Name> Rakhi Set' / '<Name> Charmlet' (100% occasion-specific). collections.json products_count field reported 145 -- checked and rejected as the known Shopify inflated-count artifact; the rendered/enumerated 84 is used.
